result_code.description: The verdict. `ISSUED_VALID` / `INDEPENDENT_VALID` mean the conditions for that target hold; the `_INVALID` forms mean they were applied and did not hold. `INCOMPLETE` means something required to decide was missing or a requested comparison could not be finished, `UNSUPPORTED` that this verifier version cannot evaluate what was presented, and `REJECTED` that the input was refused before evaluation. The taxonomy is fail-closed: the last three are not soft passes, and none of them may be read as `Independent`.

verification_target_requested.description: The target the caller asked for. `auto` lets the verifier resolve it from what the artifact carries; `issued` and `independent` assert an expected state.

verification_target_resolved.description: The target the verifier actually resolved and evaluated. Read this rather than the request when `auto` was used.

verification_target.description: The target the verdict applies to. Same value as `verification_target_resolved`; it is the member each fixture's expected result pins.

input_mode.description: How the artifacts were supplied: `package` for a single `verification_package`, `artifact_set` when the pieces were passed separately.

production_verification.description: True only when the verifier ran under the published production profile: the same system domain, root, rules domains and corpus commitments, settlement parameters and signature profile. False under any other configuration (a test domain, a synthetic root). Every signature is verified in both cases, so `false` does not mean authenticity went unchecked: it means a `*_VALID` result speaks for that other configuration, not for the production domain. Consumers must branch on this, not assume it.

domain_valid.description: The system-domain axis: the artifact is attributed to the exact expected system domain and its root binding holds, with no clone or fork accepted. An axis, not an alias of `result_code` — it reports its own plane and can be true while the overall verdict is not `*_VALID`.

rules_domain_valid.description: The rules-domain axis: the artifact resolves to the exact `rules_version` it is bound to. An axis, independent of `result_code`.

issued_valid.description: The `Issued` axis: the base certificate is structurally valid and authentic. An axis, independent of `result_code`.

independent_valid.description: The `Independent` axis: every check the independence plane requires passed, and the resolved target is `Independent`. Deliberately NOT an alias of `result_code === "INDEPENDENT_VALID"`: comparison against original material is not part of this axis, so supplying material for only some subjects makes `result_code` `INCOMPLETE` while this stays true. False on an Issued-only run, where the plane was never evaluated.

proof_complete.description: The proof is present, structurally valid, and no required artifact was missing. An axis, independent of `result_code`.

complete_verification_against_original_m.description: True when the verifier was given original material and actually ran the comparison against it. False when no material was supplied — which is not a failure: the structural planes are verifiable without it.

True when the comparison was performed and the material matched what the certificate commits to. Read together with the `_performed` flag: false with `_performed` false means the comparison never ran, not that it failed.

failure_reason.description: Human-readable reason for a non-valid verdict. Null when the verdict is valid. Diagnostic text, not a stable identifier — branch on `failed_check_ids` instead.

failed_check_ids.description: Identifiers of the checks that failed, each once. The SET is normative (verifier-toolkit/1 §9.6–§9.7); the order is evaluation order and is not compared. Every identifier is one of verifier-toolkit/1 §9.7.

required_artifacts_missing.description: Artifacts a decision required but that were not supplied. Non-empty here is why a verdict is `INCOMPLETE` rather than `*_INVALID`: nothing was disproved, something was absent.

applicable_rules_version.description: The `rules_version` the artifact is bound to and was evaluated against. Null until it has been resolved from the artifact.

system_id.description: The system domain the artifact is attributed to. Null until resolved.

system_root_identifier.description: The system root the attribution chains to. Null until resolved.

settlement_profile_id.description: Settlement profile under which capacity consumption was evidenced. Part of the lineage block: present so the binding is visible in the result rather than only inside the artifact.

subtree_root.description: Root of the subtree the artifact's commitment sits under. Lineage, visible for inspection.

settlement_ref.description: Settlement reference the operation resolved to. Lineage, visible for inspection.

batch_root.description: Root of the batch the operation settled in. Lineage, visible for inspection.

batch_index.description: Position of the operation within its batch. Lineage, visible for inspection.

batch_size.description: Number of members in the batch the operation settled in. Lineage, visible for inspection.

foundation_profile_id.description: Foundation profile of the statement that carries the system binding. Present once `system_foundation` has been validated.

foundation_statement_id.description: Identifier of the validated foundation statement. Present once it has been validated.

foundation_publication_ref.description: Publication reference of the foundation statement. Present once it has been validated.

subject_scope.description: What the verdict covers, per subject, in anchor order. A subject submitted as one opaque input (`opaque: true` — an archive or blob) is bound as that single input, and the verdict asserts nothing about elements inside it; a declared collection (`opaque: false`) is covered at the declared resolution. Proving a container is not proving its contents, and this field is what keeps the two distinguishable. Null until the base certificate is parsed.

attested_node.description: The node the Proof of Independence attests (`independence.proof/1` §10.15): the recognized node the submission entered through and the instant its recognition was checked, authenticated by the proof signature. Set only when `result_code` is `INDEPENDENT_VALID`; null otherwise and when the proof carries no attestation. It names a transport, not the issuer, and asserts nothing about the certified content.

diagnostics.description: Ordered diagnostics emitted during evaluation, each with a level and, where applicable, the check it belongs to. Informative: the verdict is `result_code`, not the absence of diagnostics.

certcrypt_lineage.description: Already-validated CERTCRYPT binding, projected into a compact consumer-readable form. A secondary view of values proven elsewhere in this result, not an independent assertion.

additional_verifications.description: Outcomes surfaced separately from the check list: the ML-DSA-65 component of the base certificate's composite signature. The component itself is normative: a certificate whose ML-DSA-65 half is absent, malformed or fails to verify does not reach `BASE_CERTIFICATE_AUTHENTIC`. This field reports that component's outcome on its own; it does not make it optional, and nothing here alters `result_code` independently of the check it belongs to.
